_comment: PHARN floor write-guards: two PreToolUse hooks on Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit. protect-trusted-paths.cjs (fix #2) blocks writes to the four trusted spec docs (CONSTITUTION/ARCHITECTURE/THREAT-MODEL/LIMITS), CODEOWNERS, git metadata (any .git path segment), and the guards' own control surface — this settings.json plus the three hook scripts, so a write can no longer disarm a guard on the next tool call; enforce-writes-scope.cjs (fix #7) blocks writes outside the active writes-scope (.pharn/writes-scope.json), fail-closed to a default-safe-set when none is set. Both run; a deny from either blocks. Both commands are anchored on the CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR placeholder ON PURPOSE: Claude Code runs a hook in Claude's CURRENT directory, so the old relative `node .claude/hooks/...` form could not start after a cd into a subdirectory — node exited 1, which is non-blocking, so both guards were silently off (measured, .dev/features/hook-cwd-anchoring). Each guard then judges the git working tree that contains Claude's current directory. A project path containing a double quote, a backtick, a dollar sign or a backslash is unsupported by this form (LIMITS.md §7). Existing installs: run `pharn update` first, then change these two commands; roll back in the reverse order. set-writes-scope.cjs additionally REFUSES to emit a scope naming the four control paths unless --allow-claude-dir is passed. .claude/commands/* and the hooks' own *.test.cjs are deliberately NOT protected. Commit this file — it is a shared guarantee. Set PHARN_PROTECTED to extend the fix #2 list. Personal, machine-local settings (e.g. permission allowlists) belong in settings.local.json, which is gitignored.
